data.long_meaning: One who is blessed by God and has divine protection. This name is derived from the Sanskrit word ‘bhagati’ which means to obtain or possess something through devotion and dedication. The name Bhagban is often given to a child born in a religious family or to one who is expected to lead a pious life. The name Bhagban carries the meaning “Blessed by God” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Bhagban usually hope their child will grow to embody blessed by god and live with faith, good character and purpose.

It is often associated with a person of high spiritual standing or who has exhibited unwavering devotion to their deity or guru. In Hindu mythology, Bhagban is also used as a term for various deities, such as Bhagvan Shri Krishna, who is considered the embodiment of divine love and compassion. This name inspires a deep reverence and respect within the Hindu community, evoking a sense of the profound connection between the individual and the divine.

historical_references.reference: Bhagban was a famous 14th century Hindu king of Malwa in central India, known for his military prowess and religious patronage. He is particularly remembered for his victory over the Muslim invader Malik Kafur in the Second Battle of Singnana in 1305 CE.

Bhagban is also known as Bhagwant Singh Tomar, and he was the founder of the Tomar Rajput Dynasty in the 11th century in the present-day Bundelkhand region. He is considered a legendary hero and is worshipped as a god by the locals.
